subject: Console request: tenant-level latency percentiles + chargeback drill
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Console request: tenant-level latency percentiles + chargeback drill

Hi team,

Quick ask from an account team escalation: Acme Payments is seeing unexpected monthly spend spikes driven by heavy tail latency on a small subset of endpoints. They asked for a self-serve view in the Console that lets them: 
- Select a tenant (or list of tenants) and see P50/P90/P95/P99 latency distributions per route
- Drill from a latency percentile into recent high-cost traces for that percentile (time window + example traces)
- Export a CSV for chargeback to their internal finance team

Acme provided a small sample CSV (attached) showing token counts and per-call latency. They want an ETA and whether this is something we can ship as a Console card + a link in the Route Inspector within 3 sprints.

Questions for product/observability:
1) Is there an existing API or query we can reuse for percentile aggregates by tenant?
2) What backend cost (query cost / indexing) concerns do we need to evaluate for per-tenant retention windows?
3) Proposed UX: a top-level "Tenant Latency" card that expands into a per-route explorer — is that feasible given current Console primitives?

I've attached a quick mockup (requested-ui-mockup.png) and Acme's sample (acme-latency-sample.csv).

Thanks,
Jordan
Director, Platform Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2029 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console request: tenant-level latency percentiles + chargeback drill

Jordan — thanks for the context and attachments, this is something we've seen a few customers ask for. Initial thoughts:

- Backend: we already materialize per-route latency histograms at ingestion (used for SLA dashboards), but not sharded by tenant at the percentile-level for arbitrary windows. We can compute percentiles on the fly via our metrics pipeline (Prometheus->OLAP) but cost will scale with cardinality.
- Short-term approach (fastest): reuse existing histograms + serve P50/P95/P99 for the last 24h/7d/30d. Put a hard cap on tenant list size in the UI (max 20 tenants) to limit query fanout.
- Mid-term: pre-aggregate tenant x route percentiles nightly (cheaper reads) and surface them in Console. Requires a small ETL job and an extra metric table.

For the UX: a Console card that links into Route Inspector is doable. Diego — can your team prototype a drill that fetches the "sample traces for percentile" (we'd need a query: SELECT traces WHERE latency >= percentile AND tenant = X) and render up to 10 example traces?

Jordan — ETA: prototype in 2 sprints for the UI + on-the-fly percentiles (restricted window/tenant count). If we go the nightly pre-aggregate route, add 1 more sprint for infra + QA. I recommend prototype first so Acme can validate.

Happy to sync with Acme if you want me on the call.

—Marissa
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acme-pay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Apr 2029 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console request: tenant-level latency percentiles + chargeback drill

Thanks Jordan & Marissa — appreciate the quick response. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The CSV is a representative week; our billing team runs monthly chargeback and needs CSV exports with the same schema you saw (route, token_count, latency_ms, timestamp, model). We don't need >30d history exposed in the UI initially, 7d would be fine.
- The demonstration of drilling from a P99 bucket into example traces is the most important piece for our SREs — they want to triage root cause and correlate to upstream spikes (network, model warm-up).
- If you can prototype a Console card and a shared link to download CSVs for selected tenants, we can validate internally next week.

Let me know when you have a short demo slot and we'll block time.

Sara Lim
SRE Lead, Acme Payments
ops@acme-pay.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Apr 2029 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console request: tenant-level latency percentiles + chargeback drill

Marissa / Jordan — quick update from infra side after reviewing JIRA OBS-1427 and the sample data: 

- Implementation plan:
  1) Short-term prototype (2 sprints): UI card + on-the-fly percentile queries restricted to 7d window + tenant cap 15. The UI will call an aggregated metrics endpoint that streams percentile values and returns a small set of example trace ids (up to 10) for the selected percentile.
  2) Export: CSV export will be generated server-side from the same trace store query (will include model and token_count schema). We will attach a signed S3 link for download.
  3) Mid-term (optional): nightly pre-aggregate job to build tenant-route percentile table for 30/90d views and cheaper reads (adds one infra sprint).

- Risk/observations: worst-case query cost under bursty scenarios could be ~2.5x current metric-query billing for accounts that exercise large tenant lists. We'll add a circuit to fail back to sampled percentile estimates if query cost > threshold.

Next steps: Marissa to scope UX; Diego to create a tech design doc and an RFC to OBS-1427; Jordan to coordinate demo timing with Acme. I'll attach the prototype API contract to the JIRA.

Diego
Engineering Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
